Healthy.name: Healthy Hibiscus Plant
Healthy.description: The plant is currently classified as healthy by the AgriGuard AI machine learning model.
symptoms: No significant leaf drying or rust-like symptoms

Leaf_Spot.name: Hibiscus Leaf Spot
Leaf_Spot.description: Leaf Spot is a condition that can cause brown, dark or discolored spots on hibiscus leaves. It may be associated with fungal or bacterial pathogens depending on the specific cause.
symptoms: Brown or dark spots on leaves
treatment: Dispose of infected plant material away from healthy plants
Improve air circulation around the plant
Use an appropriate plant disease treatment only according to its label and local agricultural guidance
prevention: Water near the soil rather than directly onto leaves

Dead_Leaf.name: Dead or Severely Damaged Leaf
Dead_Leaf.description: The AgriGuard AI model classifies the leaf as Dead_Leaf. This classification indicates significant leaf deterioration but does not by itself identify the exact underlying cause.
symptoms: Brown or completely dry leaf tissue
treatment: Inspect nearby leaves for additional symptoms
Look for signs of insects or disease

Rust.name: Hibiscus Rust
Rust.description: Rust is a fungal disease that can affect hibiscus and related plants and may produce rust-colored or yellow-orange powdery structures on affected leaves.
symptoms: Yellow or pale spots on leaves
Orange, yellow, brown or rust-colored fungal structures
Discoloration on the underside of leaves
Premature leaf drop in severe cases
treatment: Dispose of infected plant material properly
Keep foliage as dry as practical
Use a suitable fungicide only according to its label and local agricultural guidance
